title: Parse a Server-Sent Events Stream
statement:
Chat model APIs stream their answers as server-sent events (SSE): plain text, one field per line, events separated by a blank line. Your product reads the stream and shows tokens as they arrive. Write the parser.

Write def solution(stream). stream is a string. Lines end with " ". Any text after the last " " is an unfinished line: ignore it. Read the complete lines in order, keeping a current event that starts with name "message" and no data lines:

  • Blank line (empty string): the event ends. If it has at least one data line, emit [name, data] where data is its data lines joined with " ". Either way, start a fresh event (name "message", no data).
  • Comment: a line starting with : is ignored.
  • Field: otherwise split the line at its first : into a field and a value. If the value starts with a space, remove that one space (data: x and data:x both give x; data: x gives x). A line with no colon is a field with an empty value.
  • data adds the value as a data line, except data: [DONE], which stops parsing at once: it is not emitted, the event in progress is dropped, and nothing after it is read.
  • event sets the event's name; an empty value sets it back to "message". Any other field (id, retry, ...) is ignored.

An event that is still open when the stream ends was cut off, so it is not emitted. Return the list of [event_name, data] pairs in order.

examples.why: Two events with one data line each, both named message. [DONE] ends the stream and is not emitted.

examples.input:
stream = "event: delta
data: line one
data: line two

: keep-alive

data:x

data: cut off"
examples.why: The first event is named delta and has two data lines, joined with \n. The comment line is skipped and its blank line ends an event with no data, so nothing is emitted. data:x has no space after the colon and still gives x. data: cut off has no newline after it: unfinished, ignored.

constraints: field names are case-sensitive: Data: is not data

think.q: What state survives from one line to the next?
think.a: The current event: its name and its list of data lines. Blank lines flush it; everything else edits it. The output is a list of flushed events.

Split on \n: ["event: a", "data: 1", "", "data: 2", ""]. The last piece is the text after the final newline (empty here) and is dropped. Line 3 flushes ["a", "1"]. data: 2 is never followed by a blank line, so it is not emitted.

think.q: What's the first thing you'd write?
think.a: Split on " " into events, then split each on " ". It looks shorter but gets the edges wrong: leaves stray empty lines, the unfinished tail looks like a full event, and [DONE] handling spreads across two loops. One pass over lines is clearer.

"line", "field", "blank line ends the event" → a line-by-line state machine over strings. Each line falls into exactly one case: blank, comment, or field: value. line.split(':', 1) splits at the first colon only, so JSON payloads with colons survive.

1. lines = stream.split('\n'), then drop the last piece (unfinished).
  2. name, data = 'message', [].
  3. Blank: emit if data, then reset. : first: skip.
  4. Else split at the first colon, strip one leading space.
  5. data: stop on [DONE], else append. event: set the name.

Empty stream. Only blank lines. Missing final blank line. No newline at all. data:x vs data: x. A bare data line. A colon inside the data. [DONE] in the middle of an event. A name from a dataless event leaking into the next one.

hints: stream.split('\n') always returns one more piece than there are newlines. The last piece is the unfinished line: lines.pop() it.
Use field, value = line.split(':', 1) when the line has a colon, then if value.startswith(' '): value = value[1:]. Do not use strip(): it would remove spaces the model actually sent.
Reset both the name and the data list on every blank line, even when you do not emit. Otherwise an event: ping with no data renames the next event.
explain:
The parser is a loop over complete lines with a tiny state: name and data. Every line is one of three things, and the order of the checks matters: blank first, then comment, then field.

  • Example 2: event: delta sets the name. Two data lines give ["line one", "line two"]. The blank line emits ["delta", "line one\nline two"] and resets.
  • : keep-alive is a comment. The next blank line finds no data, so nothing is emitted (servers send these to keep idle connections open).
  • data:x splits into data and x; there is no space to remove. The next blank line emits ["message", "x"].
  • data: cut off is the piece after the last newline, popped before the loop.

Why this matters in a product: network chunks do not line up with events. A chunk can end mid-line, so a streaming client keeps the unfinished tail in a buffer and prepends it to the next chunk. Dropping the tail here is the same rule, applied once at the end.

perf.label: performance: 20,000 token events in one stream
perf.gen:
[''.join('data: tok%d

' % i if i % 50 else 'event: tick
: ka
data: %d
data: x

' % i for i in range(20000)) + 'data: [DONE]

']

govtech.evidence: Practice shaped like the lab's public products (streamed answers in GovBrain and Transcribe X); not a reported interview question.
extensions: Make it incremental: a Parser class with feed(chunk) that returns the events completed by that chunk. Chunks can split a line, or even [DO / NE], anywhere.
Accept \r\n and lone \r line endings too, as the SSE spec does. Where do you normalise so the rest of the parser does not change?
Each data is a JSON chunk like {"delta": "Hel"}. Concatenate the deltas into the final answer text, and skip (but count) chunks that fail to parse.
Track the last id: field so a dropped connection can reconnect with Last-Event-ID and resume. Which events should the client de-duplicate after a resume?

tests.why: id/retry are ignored; event: with no value resets to message; only the first colon splits
